newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals futures end mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals futures end mostly up.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended mostly up on Friday, buoyed by slight yen weakness and firmer spot prices, traders said.

Gold prices ranged from seven to nine yen per gram higher, with most-active benchmark October ending up nine yen at 1,334 yen. Platinum prices ranged from four to seven yen per gram up. Benchmark October was up five yen at 1,339 yen.

Activity in gold futures was lacklustre. In the bullion market, attempts to break above $370 failed during Asian hours. Gold was quoted at $369.70/370.00 at the Tokyo close, against the New York close of $368.90/369.40 on Thursday.

A fall in the U.S. stock market provided support to the bullion market, the traders said. "Trading in the bullion market is expected to be nervous, as it watches closely the U.S. stock market. But any price rebound led by short-covering could be capped by possible selling from Australian producers," one dealer at a foreign bank said.
In gold futures, private investors were liquidating their positions in nearby months ahead of the spot expiry next week, while making fresh purchases in distant months.
In the spot platinum market, speculative buying lifted platinum up to $370.00/75 during Asian hours.

Palladium futures were mixed. "Some palladium futures on TOCOM were pressured by profit-taking at around 430 yen. But in the spot palladium market, buying interest from overseas investors was quite strong," one trader said.
The trader said palladium prices are likely to firm, supported by a delay in Japan's year-end talks with Russia on export contracts for platinum group metals.
Traders expect Russia's January deliveries of platinum group metals to Japan to be cancelled or postponed.
Benchmark palladium October was flat at 429 yen. Benchmark silver October was 0.2 yen per 10 grams down at 177.5 yen.
